summary: Sebastian Nehrdich works in computational studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at the University of Hamburg (attested 2019) and was an exchange student at Kyoto University. He is a research fellow at Hamburg (attested 2024–2026).
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed his studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi is a historian who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She taught at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1991–1994) and the University of Delhi (~2008–2020), and served as professor of history at Jamia Millia Islamia (~1994–2008) and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo Fine Arts School (~1889–1893) under Umpei Shinma and Kanō Tomonobu, later serving there as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905).

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar in archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928, DLitt 1962) under Kosaku Hamada. He held posts at the Academy of Oriental Culture's Kyoto Institute and was professor at Kyoto University (1949–1968).

Seiichi Yagi (born 1932) is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968–1993), Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his degrees from the University of Tokyo (~1914–1917, LLD 1933) under Eiichi Makino. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later held posts there (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008) and became an associate professor there around 2013.

Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2001–2015).
Seiji Tanaka (1897–1994) was a scholar who studied under Bruno Petzold. During his career, he held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University and Asia University.
Seijun Ishii (born 1958) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University from ~1977 to 1981 and became a professor there around 2003.

Seikaku Hirata (1924–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1946–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki, and later held an academic post at Hanazono University.

Seiki Kudo (born 1931) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held academic positions as an assistant at Kyoto University and as an assistant professor at both Shuchiin University and Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Sein Tin (1899–1942) was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1921–1927) under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927) and continued his studies at Christ Church, University of Oxford (~1927–1930).
Seiran Ouchi (1845–1918) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a tutor at Nishi Hongan-ji and later served as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

Seiren Matsunami (born 1903) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1938). He held professorships at Kyushu University (~1952–1967) and Rissho University (~1969–1974).

Seishi Karashima (1957–2019) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University. He was a researcher at the Eastern Institute and later professor and director at IRIAB, Soka University (~1996–2019).

Seishin Kato (1872–1956) was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), president of Taisho University (1940), and president of Toyo University (1952, 1955).
